item.title: ZBloggers Monitor · Thursday 2 July 2026 — Massive overnight strike on Kyiv dominates; Ukraine hits Russian regions with 460 drones
item.description:
ZBloggers Monitor

Thursday 2 July 2026 — daily read on 10 pro-Kremlin military Telegram channels

The monitored channels overwhelmingly foregrounded a large combined missile-and-drone strike on Kyiv and other Ukrainian regions, celebrated as retaliation targeting weapons plants and energy infrastructure, while a major Ukrainian drone barrage on Russian regions drove the day's sharpest negative sentiment.

🚩 Frontline sentiment jumps to fully positive. Frontline net sentiment rose 28 points to +100 as channels amplified claimed advances toward Konstantinovka, capture of Kopani and Piskunovka, and progress on the Hulyaipole direction.

🚩 Ukraine-strikes sentiment collapses 66 points. Coverage of Ukraine's claimed 460-drone barrage, the Kstovo refinery fire, the Stockholm embassy incident and the border bus attack drove net sentiment down to -75.

🚩 Watchlist topics silent. No posts on mobilisation rumours or criticism of Putin were recorded today; the only 'criticism' posts targeted Ukrainian military claims, not the Russian leadership.

  1. Channels tout massive combined strike on Kyiv and beyond (✓ multiple channels)
    Two Majors, Rybar and others claimed a large overnight strike on Kyiv, Kharkiv and Dnipro using cruise missiles, Iskander-M, hypersonic Zircons and Geran drones, causing power outages across five regions and water disruption in Odesa. Two Majors cited figures of 74 missiles and 496 drones; WarGonzo gave a lower count of 60+ missiles and 100+ drones. All figures are channel/MoD-sourced and unconfirmed. source ↗
  2. Strikes framed as hits on Ukrainian weapons production (✓ multiple channels)
    Poddubny and Kotsnews claimed the strike destroyed plants producing Flamingo missiles, Neptune rockets and Lutyi drones, naming the Kiev Radio Plant, Radionics and Antonov facilities. Claims are unverified and serve to justify strikes as military-industrial targeting. source ↗
  3. Ukraine launches large drone barrage on Russian regions (✓ multiple channels)
    Arkhangel Spetsnaza claimed Ukraine launched 460 drones on regions including Leningrad, Nizhny Novgorod and Stavropol; Two Majors reported the Kstovo oil refinery hit and fires, while also claiming air defenses downed 327 drones. Figures are MoD/channel-sourced and unconfirmed; this drove the day's negative sentiment spike. source ↗
  4. Channels amplify drone attack on border bus and Stockholm embassy (✓ multiple channels)
    Multiple channels reported a Ukrainian drone striking a civilian passenger bus at the Belarus-Russia border, wounding two and closing a checkpoint, and a paint/mock-bomb attack on the Russian embassy in Stockholm. Framed to emphasize alleged Ukrainian targeting of civilians and diplomatic sites. source ↗
  5. Frontline claims: advances toward Konstantinovka and Hulyaipole (✓ multiple channels)
    Sladkov+ and Two Majors framed Konstantinovka as the main Russian concentration point and springboard, while WarGonzo claimed control of Kopani and advances near Iskra on Hulyaipole; Kotsnews claimed the capture of Piskunovka. All are unconfirmed channel claims and drove a strongly positive frontline mood. source ↗

Mood of coverage: 59% positive / 4% neutral / 37% negative across 49 substantive posts.

item.title: ZBloggers Monitor · Wednesday 1 July 2026 — Kopani and Ukrainske captured; Ukraine hits Crimea, fuel-strike campaign widens
item.description:
ZBloggers Monitor

Wednesday 1 July 2026 — daily read on 10 pro-Kremlin military Telegram channels

Pro-Kremlin channels celebrated claimed captures of Kopani (Zaporizhzhia) and Ukrainske (Kharkiv) alongside an escalating campaign against Ukrainian fuel infrastructure, while an unusually negative note ran through coverage of Ukrainian drone strikes on Crimea and Russian rear regions and persistent domestic fuel-shortage warnings.

🚩 Ukraine strikes on Russia mood drops 62 points. Sentiment on Ukrainian strikes fell to net -9 as channels reported Crimean power outages in Armyansk and Feodosia, an OMON officer killed in Kursk, and a claimed 300-drone overnight barrage.

🚩 Russia internal mood collapses 80 points. Coverage turned sharply negative (net -60) on persistent fuel-shortage warnings tied to Trump-Putin talks and infrastructure terrorism, plus Omsk warnings of insider drone attacks 2,500km from the front.

🚩 Watchlist topics silent. No posts on mobilisation rumours or direct criticism of Putin; domestic grievances stayed focused on fuel supply and MoD reporting rather than leadership.

  1. Claimed capture of Kopani in Zaporizhzhia widely reported (✓ multiple channels)
    Multiple channels claimed Russian marines liberated Kopani, reporting two Ukrainian platoons destroyed and a wedge forming toward Orekhovsk/Orekhov. Claims are channel-sourced and unconfirmed; the consistency across outlets suggests a coordinated messaging push. source ↗
  2. Ukrainske village claimed captured near Volchansk/Kupyansk (✓ multiple channels)
    Channels reported Russian forces took Ukrainske south of Volchansk on the Burluk direction, claiming a broken Ukrainian defensive line and expanded security zone. Unconfirmed and MoD-aligned framing. source ↗
  3. Fuel-infrastructure strike campaign framed as systematic (✓ multiple channels)
    Rybar claimed drones struck over 70 Ukrainian gas stations, mostly in Kharkiv, with further strikes reported across Dnipropetrovsk, Poltava, and Zaporizhzhia. One blogger (Starshe Eddy) criticized strikes as too one-off, urging systematic destruction — a rare intra-camp critique. Claims unconfirmed. source ↗
  4. Ukrainian strikes hit Crimea energy and Russian regions (✓ multiple channels)
    Channels reported 300 Ukrainian drones launched overnight (179 claimed downed), power knocked out in Armyansk and Feodosia with rolling Crimean blackouts, and an OMON bomb-disposal officer killed in Kursk. This drove the day's negative sentiment spike on the topic. source ↗
  5. Konstantinovka: Ukrainian garrison abandoned, channels claim (✓ multiple channels)
    Arkhangel Spetsnaza claimed Ukraine's command deliberately abandoned the surrounded Konstantinovka garrison to hold Kramatorsk-Slavyansk, while Poddubny reported Russian mopping-up. Kotsnews noted Ukraine preparing Sloviansk/Kramatorsk for urban warfare. Unconfirmed. source ↗

Mood of coverage: 54% positive / 12% neutral / 34% negative across 74 substantive posts.

item.title: ZBloggers Monitor · Tuesday 30 June 2026 — Zaporizhzhia villages fall as Ukraine drone barrage kills infant
item.description:
ZBloggers Monitor

Tuesday 30 June 2026 — daily read on 10 pro-Kremlin military Telegram channels

Pro-Kremlin channels celebrated the reported capture of Rovnoe, Lesnoe and Malinovka on the Hulyaipole axis while amplifying grief and outrage over a mass Ukrainian drone attack that they say killed a six-month-old in Egorievsk. Sentiment split evenly, with sharp negative swings on Ukrainian strikes and Western rearmament.

🚩 Ukraine strikes on Russia dives to -71. Sentiment fell 38 points as channels amplified a 590-drone attack and the reported killing of a six-month-old in Egorievsk, dominating the day's negative coverage.

🚩 West & NATO drops to -70. A 40-point negative swing driven by EU's 3.9bn euro drone tranche, a new Germany-Netherlands NATO command center in Estonia, and European rearmament announcements framed as anti-Russian escalation.

🚩 Mobilisation rumours and Putin criticism absent. Watchlist items 'Mobilisation rumours' and 'Criticism of Putin' saw no posts; criticism instead targeted government perception management, Ukrainian conscription and the Monaco bombing case.

  1. Channels claim capture of Rovnoe, Lesnoe, Malinovka in Zaporizhzhia (✓ multiple channels)
    At least six channels reported Russian Eastern Forces seized Rovnoe, Lesnoe and Malinovka across the Zaporizhzhia/Donetsk border, with claims of a breakthrough near Vozdvizhenka. Poddubny and Arkhangel Spetsnaza also cite gains near Pokrovsk including Novoselkovka. Unconfirmed and not independently verified. source ↗
  2. Mass Ukrainian drone attack; infant reported killed in Egorievsk (✓ multiple channels)
    Channels report Ukraine launched 590 drones, with 419 intercepted across ten regions and 50-60 over the Moscow area. Multiple channels emphasise a six-month-old child killed and mother mortally wounded in Egorievsk. Figures are MoD-aligned/unconfirmed; the child's death drove heavy negative sentiment. source ↗
  3. Continued campaign against Ukrainian fuel and power infrastructure (✓ multiple channels)
    Channels claim Geran/Geranium drones and Su-34 strikes destroyed 25 gas stations and fuel depots and hit 154 kV power lines near Zaporizhzhia, disabling metal plants and defence manufacturers. Rybar tempers claims, saying only 23% of Kharkiv fuel infrastructure has been targeted. Unconfirmed. source ↗
  4. Sharp negative turn on Western rearmament and NATO in Estonia (✓ multiple channels)
    Channels flagged EU's 3.9bn euro first tranche for Ukrainian drones (of a 90bn package), a new Germany-Netherlands NATO command center in Estonia, Netherlands' 27bn euro budget/100k army plan, Romania's 2bn euro Spyder buy and Lithuania's proposal to lift its ban on foreign bases and nukes. Framed as a Western strategy to destroy Russia. source ↗
  5. NgP raZVedka pushes Crimea amphibious landing narrative (◌ single source)
    NgP raZVedka claims Ukraine has long planned an amphibious landing near Yalta, exploiting Russian restraint over striking civilian areas. Single-source, unverified — appears aimed at justifying looser targeting rules in Crimea. source ↗

Mood of coverage: 44% positive / 12% neutral / 44% negative across 75 substantive posts.

item.title: ZBloggers Monitor · Monday 29 June 2026 — Geran fuel-depot strikes surge; 209 Ukrainian drones claimed downed
item.description:
ZBloggers Monitor

Monday 29 June 2026 — daily read on 10 pro-Kremlin military Telegram channels

Pro-Kremlin channels celebrated an intensified Geran drone campaign against Ukrainian fuel and gas infrastructure while touting a claimed 209-drone overnight air-defense haul, even as Ukrainian strikes hit Russian energy sites. Frontline mood stayed buoyant on reported gains in Dnipropetrovsk and around Konstantinovka.

🚩 Strikes on Ukraine sentiment maxes out (+42). All 16 posts on strikes were positive, pushing net to +100 as channels lionized the Geran campaign against fuel depots in Kirovohrad and gas facilities in Kharkiv.

🚩 Ukraine-strikes mood rebounds (+56). Still net-negative (-33), the topic swung upward as channels foregrounded the claimed 209-drone intercept and mobile-fire-group successes rather than damage.

🚩 Russia-internal mood drops (-57). Net fell to +18 as posts on threatened mobile fire groups, missing medical kits and mobilisation offset upbeat coverage of Beloussov's anti-drone strategy.

🚩 Mobilisation chatter across three channels. Four posts touched mobilisation, including Belgorod's plan for eight volunteer BARS air-defense battalions and warnings about undertrained, under-equipped mobile fire groups needing first-aid kits.

🚩 No criticism of Putin. The watchlist recorded zero posts directly criticizing Putin; the day's limited criticism targeted military planning and government intelligence framing instead.

  1. Geran strikes hammer Ukrainian fuel and gas infrastructure (✓ multiple channels)
    Channels claimed Geran-4/5 drones destroyed fuel depots in Kirovohrad and gas-distribution facilities in Kharkiv (including the Skvorcovskaya site), framing strikes as reaching a "new effectiveness level." All claims are channel/MoD-sourced and unconfirmed. source ↗
  2. Russia claims 209 Ukrainian drones downed overnight (✓ multiple channels)
    Multiple channels amplified an MoD claim of 209 drones destroyed over several regions, with Sevastopol reporting 29 shot down and minor debris damage. Ukrainian strikes still hit energy infrastructure in Zaporizhzhia and Kherson; the top post drew 553k views. source ↗
  3. Claimed advances at Bogodiarovka and Konstantinovka retreat (✓ multiple channels)
    Channels reported the 36th Guards brigade and Eastern/Vostok groups capturing Bogodiarovka in Dnipropetrovsk direction and a claimed Ukrainian retreat from Konstantinovka. Rybar claimed a fourth settlement seized along the Gaichur river. All unconfirmed. source ↗
  4. Armed Gazprom tanker framed as shadow-fleet deterrent (✓ multiple channels)
    Channels highlighted the LNG tanker Marshal Vasilevsky fitted with Kord machine guns in the Gulf of Finland, citing a purported NATO strategist to argue arming shadow-fleet vessels deters European boarding operations. source ↗
  5. Belgorod plans eight volunteer BARS air-defense battalions (◌ single source)
    Two Majors reported a Belgorod deputy governor announcing plans to form eight volunteer BARS battalions for air defense (135k views), part of a cluster of mobilisation-related posts flagged by the monitor. source ↗

Mood of coverage: 47% positive / 23% neutral / 30% negative across 77 substantive posts.

item.title: ZBloggers Monitor · Sunday 28 June 2026 — Putin talks up advances as Ukrainian drones hit refineries
item.description:
ZBloggers Monitor

Sunday 28 June 2026 — daily read on 10 pro-Kremlin military Telegram channels

Channels amplified an extensive Putin briefing claiming gains across all fronts and rejecting ceasefire proposals, while sentiment soured sharply over a coordinated Ukrainian drone campaign on Russian refineries and fuel shortages. Unusually, the same channels ran heavy criticism of official Russian media for downplaying the war.

🚩 Fuel-strike anxiety deepens (-89, down 39). Sentiment on Ukrainian strikes fell sharply as channels reported a coordinated drone campaign against refineries, the Slavyansk-on-Kuban fire, and admitted fuel shortages affecting millions — with even Putin acknowledging Crimea's 70K-ton monthly fuel need.

🚩 Russia-internal mood jumps to +75. A rare strong positive swing driven by the 'Citadel' anti-drone system rollout, parliament cutting the rifle-ownership waiting period from five to three years, and Putin's unity messaging.

🚩 Mobilisation and Putin-criticism watchlists quiet. Mobilisation surfaced only via Belgorod's eight new BARS battalions, not federal call-ups, and direct criticism targeted media and army command rather than Putin, who was quoted approvingly throughout.

  1. Putin frontline briefing amplified across channels (✓ multiple channels)
    Multiple channels relayed a detailed Putin update claiming Russian advances in all directions, movement toward Slavyansk, breached fortifications by the Center group, and that liberating Donbas and 'Novorossiya' remains required. He called Ukrainian ceasefire offers 'unacceptable' and said such proposals come from the losing side (channel framing, MoD/Kremlin-sourced). source ↗
  2. Ukrainian drone strikes on refineries drive sentiment down (✓ multiple channels)
    Channels reported a 'coordinated' Ukrainian drone campaign against Russian refineries, with a 20,000+ sq m fire at the Slavyansk-on-Kuban refinery, one killed in Krasnodar, and claims of fuel production losses and regional shortages. Russian MoD claimed 213+ drones intercepted overnight (unconfirmed). Mood on this topic swung to -89 (down 39). source ↗
  3. Claimed captures of Novoseloka and Pisantsy (✓ multiple channels)
    Channels claimed Russia's Vostok group and 38th/36th brigades took Novoseloka (eastern Zaporizhzhia, toward Orekhovsk) and Pisantsy plus Novoskelyvatoe in the Dnipropetrovsk direction, alongside clearing near Rai-Aleksandrovka and Konstantinovka (channel/MoD claims, unconfirmed). source ↗
  4. 'Citadel' air defense system unveiled against drones (✓ multiple channels)
    Several channels promoted Russia's new short-range 'Citadel' air defense system with programmable ammunition to protect critical infrastructure from drone attacks — driving Russia-internal sentiment to +75. Timing aligns with fuel-infrastructure vulnerability messaging. source ↗
  5. Sharp criticism of Russian media and authorities (✓ multiple channels)
    Rybar and Two Majors ran a critical cluster: federal media downplaying casualties and failing to attribute infrastructure damage to Ukrainian strikes, and authorities prosecuting civilians who film drone strikes. Two Majors and Sladkov also faulted absent layered air defense and poor dispersal/ammo storage discipline. source ↗

Mood of coverage: 46% positive / 22% neutral / 32% negative across 65 substantive posts.

item.title: ZBloggers Monitor · Saturday 27 June 2026 — Novoskelvatoe seized near Pokrovsk; Rybar slams fuel-strike coordination
item.description:
ZBloggers Monitor

Saturday 27 June 2026 — daily read on 10 pro-Kremlin military Telegram channels

Pro-Kremlin channels amplified a strong frontline day—claimed capture of Novoskelvatoe and a bridgehead west of the Gaichur river toward Pokrovsk—while Rybar broke ranks to call Russia's strikes on Ukrainian fuel infrastructure poorly coordinated and insufficient. Sentiment on the frontline surged, but a Ukrainian strike on a WW2 memorial museum in Rostov drew angry coverage.

🚩 Frontline sentiment jumps +33 to net +95. Near-unanimous positive posting driven by the claimed capture of Novoskelvatoe, a Gaichur bridgehead toward Pokrovsk, and repeated Leopard/howitzer/locomotive kill claims.

🚩 Strikes on Ukraine drops 39 points to net +50. Rybar's multi-post critique calling fuel-infrastructure strikes insufficient and poorly coordinated pulled an otherwise upbeat topic down despite MiG-29 and substation strike claims.

🚩 West & NATO falls 46 points to net -67. Sentiment soured on Sweden's coast-guard militarization to 2030, Ukraine's stated ballistic-missile plans against Moscow and St. Petersburg, and the unusually secretive Putin-Lukashenko meeting.

🚩 Mobilisation rumours and Putin criticism absent. No posts on mobilisation rumours or direct criticism of Putin; the day's criticism was limited to two posts targeting authorities' drone messaging and museum funding.

  1. Claimed capture of Novoskelvatoe, bridgehead toward Pokrovsk (✓ multiple channels)
    Multiple channels claimed Russia's Vostok grouping liberated Novoskelvatoe and established a bridgehead west of the Gaichur river, framing it as a springboard for the Pokrovsk advance in the Dnipropetrovsk direction. Unconfirmed; channel-sourced, not attributed to MoD. source ↗
  2. Rybar criticizes Russia's own fuel-strike campaign as inadequate (◌ single source)
    In a notable self-critical thread, Rybar argued strikes on Ukrainian fuel bases in Dnipropetrovsk were insufficient and poorly coordinated, and that Russia has not destroyed southern fuel infrastructure, while separately arguing 22 Odesa oil depots could cripple Ukrainian logistics if targeted. source ↗
  3. Claimed destruction of two MiG-29s at Voznesensk airfield (✓ multiple channels)
    Several channels claimed Russian Shahed/Geran loitering munitions destroyed two Ukrainian MiG-29 fighters, plus fuel trucks and personnel, at Voznesensk airfield in Mykolaiv region. Unconfirmed. source ↗
  4. Ukrainian strike on Rostov WW2 memorial museum drives outrage (✓ multiple channels)
    Channels reported a Ukrainian drone strike on the Sambekskie Heights military museum in Rostov region during a festival, damaging the WW2 memorial complex and injuring twelve, used to frame Ukraine as targeting civilian/heritage sites. source ↗
  5. Leopard tank claimed destroyed near Konstantinovka by FPV drones (✓ multiple channels)
    Multiple channels claimed coordinated FPV drone strikes destroyed a camouflaged German Leopard tank near Konstantinovka, amid reported Russian clearing operations there. Unconfirmed. source ↗

Mood of coverage: 54% positive / 20% neutral / 26% negative across 54 substantive posts.

item.title: ZBloggers Monitor · Friday 26 June 2026 — Rail-interdiction strike wave; Crimea declares emergency after drone barrage
item.description:
ZBloggers Monitor

Friday 26 June 2026 — daily read on 10 pro-Kremlin military Telegram channels

Channels celebrated a coordinated Geran-drone campaign against Ukrainian railways and refineries while grappling with a record Ukrainian drone attack that forced Crimea and Sevastopol into an emergency regime and produced rare admissions of Ukrainian advances on the Zaporizhzhia front.

🚩 Frontline sentiment cools 29 points. Rybar's admission of 'unfavorable dynamics' and Ukrainian advances near Kamenske, Primorske and Hulyaipole pulled the frontline net score down to +62, tempering otherwise upbeat Konstantinovka and Red Liman claims.

🚩 Ukraine-strikes topic drops 35 points. A record Ukrainian drone attack on Crimea, Moscow, Tula and Vladimir regions — with Sevastopol grid damage and an emergency regime declared — drove sentiment to net -62.

🚩 West & NATO sentiment rebounds 29 points. Coverage of German F126 frigate cost overruns, a sympathetic Scott Ritter Donbas visit and Hormuz-Strait disruption lifted the topic's net to -21 despite Western aid concerns.

🚩 Mobilisation and Putin-criticism threads dormant. Watchlist items 'Mobilisation rumours' and 'Criticism of Putin' saw no substantive posts; governance criticism instead targeted Rostechnadzor and private-sector refinery protection, not the leadership directly.

  1. Geran drones claimed to destroy five locomotives in rail-interdiction push (✓ multiple channels)
    Multiple channels amplified claims that Geran-2 drones destroyed five trains/locomotives at the Malynivka-Lozova hub on the Kharkiv-Zaporizhzhia border, framing it as a shift toward systematic railway interdiction. Rybar claimed increasing video confirmation of locomotive strikes; all figures are channel/MoD-sourced and unverified. source ↗
  2. Record Ukrainian drone attack forces Crimea emergency regime (✓ multiple channels)
    Channels reported a large Ukrainian drone strike on Crimea, Moscow, Tula and Vladimir regions, with Sevastopol power grid damage and a claimed 84 drones downed over Tula. Crimea and Sevastopol declared an emergency regime — described variously as security-driven and as a mechanism to accelerate federal budget aid. All casualty and interception figures unconfirmed. source ↗
  3. Rybar admits 'unfavorable dynamics' on Zaporizhzhia front (◌ single source)
    Rybar reported Ukrainian forces advancing southward near Kamenske and Hulyaipole, allegedly occupying Primorske and pressuring Plavni — a rare negative frontline admission driving the topic's 29-point mood drop. Other channels countered with upbeat claims (Konstantinovka clearance, 763 structures/560+ soldiers per Kotsnews); numbers unverified. source ↗
  4. Prisoner exchange returns 160 Russian soldiers (✓ multiple channels)
    Channels widely reported a 160-for-160 prisoner swap with Ukraine, with Rybar claiming over 1,500 Russians returned since 2025. Framed positively with mentions of medical and rehabilitation support. source ↗
  5. Bloggers blame Rostechnadzor, private sector for refinery fires (✓ multiple channels)
    Two Majors and NgP raZVedka aired industry complaints that Rostechnadzor delays refinery security upgrades and that unclear federal-versus-private protection responsibility enables repeat Ukrainian strikes — a rare governance-critical thread amid claimed battlefield successes. source ↗

item.title: ZBloggers Monitor · Thursday 25 June 2026 — Russia touts fuel-strike campaign as Crimea reels from Ukrainian attacks
item.description:
ZBloggers Monitor

Thursday 25 June 2026 — daily read on 10 pro-Kremlin military Telegram channels

Pro-Kremlin channels celebrated an intensified campaign against Ukrainian gas stations and fuel logistics while grappling with a sharp mood downturn over Ukrainian drone strikes on Crimea that killed civilians and caused energy shortages.

🚩 Crimea attacks flip sentiment on Ukrainian strikes. Net sentiment on Ukraine strikes on Russia moved 43 points to -27 as channels reported civilian deaths near Dzhankoy, Sevastopol power restrictions, water and fuel shortages and reduced rail service across the peninsula.

🚩 Mobilisation and Putin criticism absent. Watchlisted topics 'Mobilisation rumours' and 'Criticism of Putin' saw no posts today; internal criticism instead targeted refinery owners, bureaucracy and army command.

  1. Channels tout escalating strikes on Ukrainian fuel network (✓ multiple channels)
    Multiple channels claimed Russian Geran/Geranium drones are now systematically hitting Ukrainian gas stations, fuel trucks and depots rather than depleted refineries, with Rybar asserting the pace exceeds April-May levels. Claims are channel-sourced and unverified; framed as a coordinated anti-logistics campaign amid a Ukrainian fuel crisis. source ↗
  2. Ukrainian strikes on Crimea drive sharp mood downturn (✓ multiple channels)
    Channels reported a child and adult killed near Dzhankoy, emergency power restrictions in Sevastopol, water shortages and reduced rail service; Arkhangel Spetsnaza cited 514 drones downed in 24 hours (MoD-adjacent, unconfirmed). Sentiment on this topic swung 43 points negative despite Russia's own strike gains. source ↗
  3. Konstantinovka push framed as gateway to Kramatorsk (✓ multiple channels)
    Kotsnews and WarGonzo claimed Russian forces are penetrating the 'fortress city' of Konstantinovka, cutting garrison supply lines, citing a Telegraph report that NATO fears Moscow aims at Kramatorsk and Slavyansk. Advances in Orikhiv and Zaporizhzhia directions also claimed; all unconfirmed. source ↗
  4. Rare self-criticism over refinery defense failures (✓ multiple channels)
    Two Majors demanded private refinery owners lose assets over inadequate wartime protection and blamed outdated 2014 laws and a May 2024 decree making fire-safety standards voluntary; Starshe Eddy criticized weak air defense specialists and passive protection. Criticism topic net sentiment was -100. source ↗
  5. Western tanker seizures condemned as 'piracy' (✓ multiple channels)
    Channels reported France detained the tanker Deliver off Sicily following a British seizure, and that Britain plans to sell seized Russian oil to fund Ukraine. Russia's embassy condemned the moves as maritime-law violations; framed as Western escalation against the shadow fleet. source ↗

Mood of coverage: 49% positive / 10% neutral / 41% negative across 82 substantive posts.
